clinician.trajectory_summary: A 26-year-old female presented with recurrent severe chest pain and heartburn since age 17. Initial laboratory tests revealed elevated inflammatory markers (CRP 1.3 mg/dL, ESR 79 mm/hour, WBC 12.8 × 10^9/L). Imaging studies confirmed extensive large vessel vasculitis, with CT showing wall thickening and narrowing of the descending thoracic and suprarenal abdominal aorta, and PET CT demonstrating significant metabolic activity (active vasculitis) in the descending aorta, subclavian, iliofemoral, and popliteal arteries. Based on these findings, treatment for vasculitis was initiated with prednisone and methotrexate.

key_supporting_evidence.claim: Patient presented with recurrent severe chest pain and heartburn, recurring intermittently since age 17.
Elevated inflammatory markers: C-reactive protein (1.3 mg/dL), erythrocyte sedimentation rate (79 mm/hour), and white blood cell count (12.8 × 10^9/L).
CT of the abdomen and pelvis demonstrated extensive wall thickening along the descending thoracic aorta and suprarenal abdominal aorta with mild narrowing of the aortic lumen.
PET CT scan revealed significant metabolic activity in the descending aorta to subclavian arteries, iliofemoral, and popliteal arteries, indicating active vasculitis.
Treatment for vasculitis was initiated with prednisone (1 mg/kg), methotrexate (20 mg weekly), and Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia prophylaxis.
